personalityFieldNotes: Per c1-integration-map.md §1.1/§1.6, PlayerPersonality carries only {archetype, motivation} and MentalAttributes carries only {awareness, decisionMaking, clutch, workEthic, coachability, leadership}. There is NO composure and NO discipline field, so every 'composure-gated' event in this file gates on MentalAttributes.clutch (the in-sim nerve stat, c1's stated composure analogue) plus Player.competitiveness (c1 §1.7: the existing adversity-response rating, and the best-fitting attribute for life-event resilience). The four convenience predicates on PlayerPersonality (isDramaticInMedia / isMentor / isMoodDependent / isConsistent) and the archetype behaviour hooks (isEgoArchetype / isFormSensitive / isFormImmune) are used as-is rather than reinvented. No field in this file is new.
availabilityNotes: Non-football injuries land on the NFI availability type, never on the medical/IR loop (c1): a club owes NO base salary while a player is on reserve/NFI, the contract year still burns, a camp-start NFI player cannot practise for 6 weeks and cannot be activated until the club has played 8 games (then a 3-week window, max 2 returns per club), and guarantees are voidable when the injury came from an enumerated significant-risk activity. Bereavement and mental-health absences use bereavementDays / personalLeave: excused absence, NO roster move, NO salary forfeit, non-punitive by construction. Three events deliberately use the ir type instead (club-organised team activities and an in-game celebration injury) because those are football/club injuries — full pay, nothing voidable — and the contrast is what makes the NFI rule legible.

targetLeagueYearVolume.notes: League = 32 teams, ~69 players/team (53+16), ~2,240 roster slots. The total is dominated by child births (~213/yr per r3 §1.4's 150-250 band), which is why the entire birth lane carries userTeamOnly: true — league-wide they would be ~200 feed items a season, on the user's own roster they are ~6. Excluding the userTeamOnly lane this file emits ~173.62 league-wide feed items per league-year, i.e. roughly 5.4 per club per season. SURFACING POLICY: the 11 userTeamOnly templates are the ones whose league-wide volume or triviality would spam the feed — the whole birth lane, a grandparent's funeral, a routine family surgery, a family relocation, a local-desk relationship note, an off-field money problem, and a wedding-turnout note. Everything else surfaces league-wide. High-volume templates that remain league-wide (engagements, weddings, bereavements, camp NFI listings) should additionally be star-gated at the FEED layer rather than at the generation layer, so the event still exists on a depth player's card without becoming a headline. SCOPE: 102 templates are player-scoped, 4 team-scoped and 7 league-scoped; the playerCard requirement applies only to player-scoped events, because a league-wide tribute or a team-wide counselling week has no single subject.

calibrationSummary: RECONCILIATION against r3-personal-life.md base rates. (1) BIRTHS: r3 §1.4 gives 150-250 births/league-year, 40-80 costing a practice, 3-10 costing a regular-season game, 1-2 becoming a national cycle. This file: 212.7 total across the childBirth subcategory (routine 138 + missed-practice 55 + gameday-decision 6.0 + national-debate 1.5 + complication 1.2 + first-child-dedication 3.0 + sleep-deprivation tail 8.0) — inside the 150-250 band, with 6.0 game-costing (inside 3-10) and 1.5 national (inside 1-2). All of it is userTeamOnly. (2) BEREAVEMENT: r3 §1.5 gives 20-40/yr affecting a player, 3-8 costing a game. This file: 37.4 across the bereavement subcategory including the tribute beat; the game-costing slice is 5.0 (missed-games) + 1.0 (crash bereavement) + 0.4 (catastrophic) = 6.4, inside 3-8. (3) NON-FOOTBALL INJURY: r3 §3.3 gives ~13 players on camp NFI at camp start, 2-5 exotic accidents costing regular-season time, 0-2 season-ending. This file: 20.97 total NFI-category events/yr, of which camp-start listings are 8.5 (rookie college injuries 6.0 + non-football illness 2.5; the campNFI subcategory totals 8.8 including its 0.3 return beat) plus the June-July mechanisms that land on the camp list (~4.5) ≈ 13.0; exotic (non camp-NFI) mechanisms whose roll can cost 4+ weeks of availability sum to 2.52-4.87 per year depending on where the roll lands, straddling the 2-5 band; season-enders (fireworks 0.12 + jet ski 0.25 + solo-workout 0.20 + rock climbing 0.12 + half the basketball Achilles 0.18) ≈ 0.87, inside 0-2. (4) PLAYER DEATHS: r3 §2.1 gives 1-3 active-or-recent deaths/yr with causes ≈50% vehicle / 25% violence incl. suicide / 15% medical / 10% overdose. This file: 2.0 across the playerDeath subcategory (vehicle 0.9 = 45%, violence 0.5 + suicide 0.3 = 40%, medical 0.3 = 15%; overdose deaths are ceded to the substances catalog to avoid double-counting), inside 1-3. (5) BURGLARY: r3 §2.5 gives a 1-3/yr baseline and a 5-10-player spike inside a ~4-month wave. This file models it as an epoch, not an i.i.d. roll: the away-game event carries 2.0/yr baseline and is multiplied ×3.5 while the organizedCrewWave flag is set; wave onset fires 0.15/yr (about once per 7 league-years) and carries its own escalation (0.9/yr in-wave repeat) and federal-charges decay beat. In-wave league volume lands at ~7 players over the flag's 20-30 week life, inside 5-10. (6) MENTAL HEALTH: r3 §4.3 gives 1-3 disclosed absences/yr and 10-25 disclosures without absence. This file: 2.6/yr of mental-health events that cost availability (stepping-away 1.2 + extended leave 0.4 + pregame scratch 1.0), inside 1-3; disclosures and programme beats without absence total 18.3 (veteran disclosure 8.0 + foundation 5.0 + peer group 2.5 + club clinician 2.0 + team-wide counselling 0.8), inside 10-25. (7) RELATIONSHIPS: r3 §1.1 gives 1-3 circus-tier couplings/yr and 10-25 engagement/wedding coverage items; this file carries 3.8/yr across the celebrityRelationship subcategory (1.6 circus onsets plus its engagement, wedding and distraction continuation beats — inside 1-3 onsets) and 34.0/yr across the engagement + wedding subcategories. That is above the top of the 10-25 band because the research band counts only NATIONALLY covered items, while this file also emits local-desk notes; the nationally-covered slice (star tier, non-userTeamOnly) is ~8/yr [E], and the low-newsworthiness templates in the lane carry userTeamOnly: true. (8) DIVORCE: r3 §1.3 gives 3-8 publicly reported divorces/yr and 0-2 in-season sagas. This file: 4.0 offseason + 1.2 in-season saga + 1.0 camp absence = 6.2, inside 3-8, with 1.2 sagas inside 0-2. The divorce subcategory totals 7.7 because custody disputes (1.5) ride in the same lane; public breakups (2.0) are counted in the relationship lane. (9) FIRE / ROBBERY / CRASH: r3 §2.3-2.6 give 1-3 house fires, 3-8 armed robberies (0-1 with injury), 5-12 serious crashes. This file: 2.5 fires, 5.3 robbery-lane (0.5 with a gunshot), 8.7 crash-lane — all inside band. FILE TOTAL: 411.62 events/league-year across 113 event templates. The total is dominated by the birth lane by design; the league-wide feed sees 173.62 items/yr once the userTeamOnly lane is excluded, i.e. roughly 5.4 per club per season.

events.body: He was twenty-four and had scored the first touchdown of his career three days earlier. Every club in the league has counsellors in the building this week. The league's confidential support line was published on every team account within the hour.

probability.calibration: r3 §2.1/§4.2: the documented worst outcome; ≈25% of deaths are firearm-related including suicide; ~0.3 per league-year

eligibility.notes: league-wide; routes directly into the team-wide counselling and mental-health lane

performance.note: team-wide for his club; -3 league-wide for one week

decision.prompt: The building is not okay. The schedule has not changed.

options.label: Cancel football for the week, counsellors only
options.followupRisk: none; also lowers the weight of every mental-health crisis roll on this roster for two seasons

options.label: Optional meetings, counsellors available all week
Normal week
options.followupRisk: mental-health crisis weight on this roster +50% for two seasons

events.designNotes: Written with no method, no detail, and a support-line beat in the body copy. The mechanical consequence is that how the club responds changes future mental-health event weights — the opposite of spectacle.

events.title: The Patch
events.headline: {TEAM} will wear a memorial patch for the rest of the season
events.body: It is small, it is on the left chest, and every player in the building can tell you exactly whose initials those are. The club will keep the locker as it is through the end of the year.

probability.calibration: r3 §2.1: helmet decals, jersey patches and season-long tribute beats follow every documented active-player death

eligibility.notes: team-scoped resolution of any death arc; runs to the end of the season

performance.note: a small, durable lift for the remainder of the season; fog-safe

events.designNotes: Turns the heaviest event in the file into a durable, quiet team effect rather than leaving it as an unresolved morale hole.

events.title: The Game Did Not Restart
events.headline: A game is suspended after a player collapses on the field
events.body: Medical staff were on him inside nine seconds and worked for ten minutes in front of seventy thousand people and both benches. He was taken to hospital in a stable condition. The league suspended the game and, later that night, announced it would not be resumed.

probability.calibration: r3 §2.2: the mass-trauma template — a regular-season game cancelled outright, both rosters counselled, seeding rules altered

eligibility.notes: league-level; both involved clubs take the arc. Overlaps the medical catalog — the on-field cause belongs there, the league-shock handling belongs here

performance.note: both involved rosters; -3 league-wide for one week

fork.headline: He is awake and asking about the game
Cleared — he intends to return next season

fork.outcome: a dormant charity of his overshoots its goal by three orders of magnitude
fork.headline: A small fundraiser in his name passes eight million dollars

playerCard.detailLine: In hospital following an on-field emergency

events.designNotes: Kept at 0.15/yr so it stays a once-a-decade dynasty memory. The charity-surge fork converts the worst moment available into the largest positive-reputation event in the game, which is exactly what the record shows.

events.title: Camp Opens Without Him
events.headline: {TEAM} open camp with {PLAYER} on the non-football injury list
events.body: The injury happened in his last college season and the club knew about it when they drafted him. He cannot practise for six weeks, cannot be activated until the club has played eight games, and then has a three-week window. Miss it and his year is over before it starts.

probability.calibration: r3 §3.3: ~13 players league-wide on NFI at camp start; most are rookies with college injuries rather than exotic accidents

eligibility.notes: rookies and second-year players; the boring majority of the NFI population

contract.note: no base salary owed while listed; the accrued season still burns

events.designNotes: Teaches the NFI rules with the lowest-stakes case. Max two returns per club per season is a roster-level constraint, not a per-event one.

events.title: Non-Football Illness
events.headline: {PLAYER} begins the season on the non-football illness list
events.body: The club has said only that he is receiving treatment and that his prognosis is good. He will finish it before he plays a down. Two teammates have already shaved their heads, which tells you more about the room than any statement would.

probability.calibration: r3 §3.2 bonus note: reserve/non-football illness is a real designation used for players finishing serious medical treatment; part of the ~13/yr camp NFI count

eligibility.notes: tier-neutral; the illness half of the camp NFI population

performance.note: fog-safe; full recovery is the norm

contract.note: no base salary obligation while listed — the club may choose to pay anyway

decision.prompt: The contract does not require you to pay him while he is on that list.

options.label: Pay him in full through the treatment
Pay the guaranteed portion only
Release and re-sign him when he is cleared
options.followupRisk: he signs elsewhere 55% of the time and the story follows the club for two seasons

playerCard.detailLine: Non-football illness list — in treatment, prognosis good

events.designNotes: The salary lever with a human face. Option (c) is legal, cheap and reputationally expensive — exactly the shape the research keeps producing.

events.body: He took his first team rep in eleven months on Wednesday and the whole defensive line stopped to watch it. He was not good. Nobody cared, including him.

events.title: Small Injury, Big Consequence
events.headline: {PLAYER} slips in a tunnel and loses two days — and maybe a job
events.body: A wet mat between drills, a tweaked knee, forty-eight hours. He was back on Thursday. By then the man behind him had taken every rep with the ones and the coaching staff had seen enough of him to change their minds.
events.contextRule: if the player is inside 3 overall points of the man above him on the depth chart, apply a permanent depth-chart demotion for the season; otherwise this is a two-day news item and nothing more

probability.calibration: r3 §3.2 mechanism 21: a minor knee injury in a tunnel between drills that cost a quarterback a depth-chart battle — the small-injury, big-career-consequence template

events.title: The Celebration
events.headline: {PLAYER} hurt celebrating his own play
events.body: He landed badly from a jump he had been planning since Tuesday. The knee buckled on the sideline in front of his own bench, roughly nine seconds after the best moment of his month.

probability.calibration: r3 §3.2 mechanism 25: torn ACL landing from a celebratory jump after a made field goal; a separate case sprained a neck head-butting a padded wall after a touchdown

events.headline: {PLAYER} will be away from {TEAM} for a personal matter

probability.calibration: r3 §4.3: publicly disclosed mental-health absences 1-3 per league-year; absences typically 2-4 games, concentrated in weeks 3-8

eligibility.notes: all tiers; a prior vague 'personal issues' flag on this player multiplies the weight sharply — the real cases almost always have a mislabelled precursor

probability.calibration: r3 §4.2: the documented precursor — pregame anxiety nearly cost a player an international game and was reported as a vague personal issue

events.title: Week Eleven Of A Four-Win Season

events.body: Asked a routine Wednesday question, he gave a much longer answer than anyone expected about what a losing season does to a person who has never had one. The room went quiet. {COACH} was asked about it an hour later and said he was glad the {POS} had said it out loud.
